AllowFile.description:
An `allow` entry as it is written on disk. The keys are in this order for a config written as a
JSON array, which serde reads by position.

lint.description:
The lint to exempt the sentence from, one of `banned_chars`, `banned_phrases`,
`verbs_no_nouns` and `not_at_all`. One entry names one lint.

path.description:
The file the sentence is in, written as a report prints it: relative to the repo root,
`/`-separated, with no glob. One entry names one file. A `path` or `reason` may not hold a
character that shows as nothing or acts on the reader: a control or format character,
another default-ignorable one, or a blank other than the ASCII space; a `reason` may hold a
tab, CR or LF.

quote.description:
The sentence, as the file holds it, without the `>` that a block quote starts its lines
with and the byte order mark that opens a file. A `>` inside a code span that wraps across
the lines of a block quote stays, and in a comment read as plain text, which is every C++
and TOML comment and a Rust comment that is not a doc comment, a `>` is text. Spaces, tabs
and line breaks fold to one space, so a sentence that is wrapped differently still matches;
a line break is LF or CR LF, or a lone CR in Markdown, while a lone CR ends a C++ `//` or
TOML `#` comment and is a character of its line in any other comment. Any other character
must match exactly, a no-break space included. The file must hold the sentence once, and
the lint must find something in it, or the entry fails the run. A `quote` may hold any
character but a control character other than a tab, CR or LF, since it must equal the
sentence, which the file holds anyway. Reports, notices and `deslag explain` write each
character that shows as nothing or acts on the reader as `<U+XXXX>`.

reason.description:
Why the sentence must stay as it is. Required. A `path` or `reason` may not hold a
character that shows as nothing or acts on the reader: a control or format character,
another default-ignorable one, or a blank other than the ASCII space; a `reason` may hold a
tab, CR or LF.

BannedChars.description:
`lints.banned_chars`: a file fails when its text outside code holds a banned character, such
as an em dash. Most have a plain character to write instead; an arrow that only a range rule
covers has none, so the report leaves the choice to the writer.

Like `repo_layout`, the table itself turns the check on: an empty one bans the groups that are
on by default. A character in `allow` is never banned; one in `ban` is banned whatever the
groups say.

allow.description: Characters that are never banned, each written as a one-character string.

ban.description:
Characters banned beyond the groups, each mapped to what to write instead. An empty
string means delete it.

groups.description: Turns groups of characters on or off.

message.description: Replaces the advice in the report. `{path}` in it is replaced with the file's path.

BannedPhrases.description:
`lints.banned_phrases`: a file fails when its prose holds a phrase of a group that is on, or a
phrase in `ban`.

Like `banned_chars`, the table itself turns the check on: an empty one bans the groups that are
on by default. A phrase matches whatever its case and its style of apostrophe, and a match
inside a match of a phrase in `allow` is not reported.

allow.description: Phrases that are never reported, such as a longer phrase that holds a banned one.

ban.description:
Banned phrases, each mapped to the advice the report shows with it. An empty string means
delete it.

groups.description: Turns groups of phrases on or off.

message.description: Replaces the advice in the report. `{path}` in it is replaced with the file's path.

CharGroups.description:
`lints.banned_chars.groups`: each group of characters switched on or off. A group left unset
is on or off as its default says.

box_drawing.description: Box-drawing characters and block elements, for `-`, `|` and `+`.

bullets.description: Bullets, the middle dot and geometric shapes, for a Markdown list's `-`.

checks.description: Check marks and crosses, for yes and no.

dashes.description: The em dash, en dash, minus sign and other dashes, for `-`.

invisible.description: Characters that do not take space, such as the zero-width space, to be deleted.

math.description: The multiplication sign and comparison signs, for `x`, `>=`, `<=`, `!=` and `~`.

quotes.description: Curly quotes and apostrophes, for `"` and `'`.

section.description: The section sign, for the word section.

spaces.description: The no-break space and other unusual spaces, for a plain space.

CommentSurface.description: The kinds of comment a section can read.

CppFile.description: The `[cpp]` section as it is written on disk.

allow.description:
The sentences of these files that stay as written, each exempted from one lint. Only a
human writes an entry. `deslag instructions lints` says how to write one.

exclude.description:
Files `globs` match that this section leaves out, such as generated code. A pattern is
written as in `globs`, from the repo root with a `/`, else by file name, and not needing a C
or C++ extension. A file the walk skips stays skipped, and nothing re-includes one. Only a
human adds an exclude; never add one to make a check pass.

globs.description:
The files this section lints. Each pattern must end in `.c`, `.h`, `.cc`, `.cpp`, `.cxx`,
`.hpp`, `.hh` or `.hxx`.

lints.description:
The settings for every selected file that no override changes. A lint that needs the whole
file, such as `max_size_bytes`, is an error here.

overrides.description: Settings for the selected files that match a pattern.

surfaces.description:
The comments this section reads, the rest of a C or C++ file being left alone.
`doc_comment` is the `///` and `//!` lines and the `/** */` and `/*! */` blocks, and the
trailing `///<` and `/**<` forms. `comment` is the other `//` lines and `/* */` blocks.
Both are read as plain text.

Density.description:
`lints.density`: a file fails when a paragraph is longer than `max_paragraph_chars`, or a list
item longer than `max_item_chars`.

Like `repo_layout`, the table itself turns the check on, with the defaults.

max_item_chars.description: The most characters a list item may hold.

max_paragraph_chars.description: The most characters a paragraph may hold.

message.description:
Replaces the advice in the report. `{path}`, `{max_paragraph_chars}` and
`{max_item_chars}` in it are replaced with the file's path and its limits.

FenceLanguage.description: The languages whose fenced code `[md]` can read.

FencesFile.description: The `fences` table of `[md]` as it is written on disk.

languages.description:
The languages whose fenced code is read: `rust`, `cpp` and `toml`. A fence is of the
language its info string names by its first word, whatever the case: `rust`, `rs`, `cpp`,
`c++`, `c`, `h`, the C and C++ extensions and `toml`. `[]` reads none.

surfaces.description:
The comments to read in a fence, for every language: `doc_comment` is the `///` and `//!`
lines and the `/** */` and `/*! */` blocks, `comment` the other `//` lines and `/* */`
blocks or, in a `toml` fence, the `#` lines. Each is read as it is in a file of its
language. `[]` turns reading off, as `languages = []` does.

Lints.description: The settings of each lint: the `lints` table of a section and of each of its overrides.

banned_chars.description: The characters the file must not hold, such as the em dash.

banned_phrases.description: The phrases the file must not hold, which the config lists.

density.description: The longest a paragraph or list item may be.

max_emphasis.description: The limit on bold, italics and ALL CAPS.

repo_layout.description: The index of the repo that the file must hold.

verbs_no_nouns.description: That a sentence negates its verb, not its object.

MaxEmphasis.description:
`lints.max_emphasis`: a file fails when it has more than `free_spans` emphasized spans and
they cover more than `max_percent` of its prose.

Setting only `free_spans` caps the number of spans; setting only `max_percent` caps their
share of the prose. A table that sets neither checks nothing.

free_spans.description: How many spans a file may have whatever share of its prose they cover.

max_percent.description: The share of the prose, in percent, that the spans may cover.

message.description:
Replaces the advice in the report. `{path}`, `{free_spans}` and `{max_percent}` in it are
replaced with the file's path and its limits.

MaxSizeBytes.description: `lints.max_size_bytes`: a file larger than `value` bytes fails.

message.description:
Replaces the advice that follows the first two lines of the report. `{path}` and
`{max_size_bytes}` in it are replaced with the file's path and budget.

value.description: The budget in bytes. A file with no budget from any source is not checked.

MdFile.description: The `[md]` section as it is written on disk.

allow.description:
The sentences of these files that stay as written, each exempted from one lint. Only a
human writes an entry. `deslag instructions lints` says how to write one.

exclude.description:
Files `globs` match that this section leaves out, such as generated code. A pattern is
written as in `globs`, from the repo root with a `/`, else by file name, and needing no
extension. A file the walk skips stays skipped, and nothing re-includes one. Only a human
adds an exclude; never add one to make a check pass.

fences.description: Which fenced code in these files is read for its comments. Overrides cannot change it.

lints.description: The settings for every selected file that no override changes.

overrides.description: Settings for the selected files that match a pattern.

NotAtAll.description:
`lints.not_at_all`: a file fails when a sentence pads a negation with "at all", as in `does not
parse at all`.

The table itself turns the check on. The negators it reads and the places it excuses are the
lint's, not the config's.

message.description: Replaces the advice in the report. `{path}` in it is replaced with the file's path.

OverrideFile.description: One entry of a section's `overrides`, as it is written on disk.

exclude.description:
Files `globs` match that this override leaves alone, so they get the section's settings.
Written as `globs` are, from the repo root with a `/`, else by file name, and needing no
extension. Nothing re-includes a file. Only a human adds an exclude; never add one to make
a check pass.

globs.description: The files this override applies to.

lints.description: The settings it lays over the section's.

PhraseGroups.description:
`lints.banned_phrases.groups`: each group of phrases switched on or off. A group left unset is
on or off as its default says.

insistence.description: Phrases that insist on what a thing does not do, such as `not silently`.

metaphors.description: Metaphors that stand in for a plain verb or claim, such as `load-bearing`.

precision.description: Words that claim a precision nobody measured, such as `byte-identical`.

RepoLayout.description:
`lints.repo_layout`: a file must have a section, under `heading`, whose first code block lists
between `min_entries` and `max_entries` paths that exist, in lines up to `max_width` wide.

Unlike the other lints, the table itself turns the check on: a file it applies to must have
the section even when the table does not set any field.

heading.description: The section's heading, matched at any level and in any case.

max_entries.description: The most entries the layout may list.

max_width.description: The widest a line of the layout may be, in characters.

message.description:
Replaces the advice in the report. `{path}`, `{heading}`, `{min_entries}`,
`{max_entries}` and `{max_width}` in it are replaced with the file's path and its settings.

min_entries.description: The fewest entries the layout may list.

RustFile.description: The `[rust]` section as it is written on disk.

allow.description:
The sentences of these files that stay as written, each exempted from one lint. Only a
human writes an entry. `deslag instructions lints` says how to write one.

exclude.description:
Files `globs` match that this section leaves out, such as generated code. A pattern is
written as in `globs`, from the repo root with a `/`, else by file name, and not needing to
end in `.rs`. A file the walk skips stays skipped, and nothing re-includes one. Only a human
adds an exclude; never add one to make a check pass.

globs.description: The files this section lints. Each pattern must end in `.rs`.

lints.description:
The settings for every selected file that no override changes. A lint that needs the whole
file, such as `max_size_bytes`, is an error here.

overrides.description: Settings for the selected files that match a pattern.

surfaces.description:
The comments this section reads, the rest of a Rust file being left alone. `doc_comment` is
the `///` and `//!` lines and the `/** */` and `/*! */` blocks, read as Markdown. `comment`
is the other `//` lines and `/* */` blocks, read as plain text.

TomlFile.description: The `[toml]` section as it is written on disk.

allow.description:
The sentences of these files that stay as written, each exempted from one lint. Only a
human writes an entry. `deslag instructions lints` says how to write one.

exclude.description:
Files `globs` match that this section leaves out, such as generated code. A pattern is
written as in `globs`, from the repo root with a `/`, else by file name, and not needing to
end in `.toml`. A file the walk skips stays skipped, and nothing re-includes one. Only a
human adds an exclude; never add one to make a check pass.

globs.description: The files this section lints. Each pattern must end in `.toml`.

lints.description:
The settings for every selected file that no override changes. A lint that needs the whole
file, such as `max_size_bytes`, is an error here.

overrides.description: Settings for the selected files that match a pattern.

surfaces.description:
The comments this section reads, the rest of a TOML file being left alone. `comment` is
the `#` lines, whole-line or after a value, read as plain text. TOML does not have another
kind of comment, so `comment` is the only value.

TomlSurface.description:
The kinds of comment `[toml]` can read. TOML does not have doc comments, so `doc_comment` is not
a value, and a config that writes it is told so.

VerbsNoNouns.description:
`lints.verbs_no_nouns`: a file fails when a sentence negates a verb through its object, as in
`bakes no cakes`.

The table itself turns the check on. The words it excuses are the lint's, not the config's.

message.description: Replaces the advice in the report. `{path}` in it is replaced with the file's path.

description: The config file as it is written on disk.

cpp.description: The C and C++ section. A config without one does not read any C or C++ file.

deslag_version.description:
The deslag that last onboarded or updated this config, as a release such as "0.0.1". When
it is missing the config is taken to be from 0.0.1. It may not be later than the deslag
that reads the file.

rust.description: The Rust section. A config without one does not read any Rust file.

schema_version.description:
The schema the file is written against, which may not be later than the one this build
reads.

toml.description: The TOML section. A config without one does not read any TOML file.
